lines.text: A quiet night. Aarav sits on the roof with a tattered book his old teacher lent him.
He thinks about duty. About what kind of person he wants to become.
I've been thinking. I don't want to spend my life chasing something I may never get. I want to find meaning in what's in front of me. My family. My craft. This neighbourhood.
That sounds like giving up with extra steps.
Giving up is when you stop wanting something because it hurts. This is different. I'm choosing what to care about.
Character planning: the deliberate, reflective cultivation of one's own desires. Aarav is forming a second-order preference — a desire about his desires.

He does not merely stop wanting engineering; he wants to stop wanting it, and he has reasons he has examined. The difficulty: from the outside, character planning and adaptive preferences look identical.
